SMTO-DB-0016 — The database search is missing a user name or password

GUID: cd74b876-61f6-4883-8e70-ec5eb767fe48
Slug: database-discovery-auth-missing
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to find the databases on a server, but it wasn't given both a user name and a password to sign in. SMTO didn't connect to anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Enter the database user name in the user field and its password in the password field. Both are required. SMTO must sign in to the server before it can list the databases on it.
  2. Keep the password only in the password field, not in the host or anywhere else in the request. Other fields can appear in logs or messages, where a password could be seen.
  3. Send the request again. Nothing was attempted the first time, so it's safe to send again once both are filled in.

What success looks like

  • The search signs in and lists the databases it found as drafts you can review.

If it still fails

  • Ask the person who manages the database for a user name and password that may list its databases. Never paste the password into a message when asking for help.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A database discovery request had an empty user (after trimming) or an empty password and was rejected as missing_user or missing_password before connecting.

What this means

  • Discovery trims the user and checks the password for emptiness, returning missing_user or missing_password before connecting. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • Discovery trims the user and checks the password for emptiness, returning missing_user or missing_password before connecting.

How to diagnose it

  • Check which private field is missing; this is not evidence of a rejected server login.

How to fix it

  • Supply both user and password in the DatabaseDiscoveryRequest's own fields; whitespace-only user values count as empty. Never embed credentials in host, a URL or any text that is logged or shown; discovery redacts them only from its own diagnostics.
  • Supply the missing fields together through the supported private credential flow. Do not put credentials in a host URL or public diagnostic.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Required private login values are supplied together without appearing in public routing text.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
